title: Bipartisan Criticism of Potential U.S. Troop Reductions in Europe
text:
• Republican and Democratic members of the House Armed Services Committee criticized reports of potential U.S. troop reductions in Europe.
• Rep. Michael Rogers, R-Mich., emphasized the importance of U.S. leadership in NATO and opposed any troop cuts.
• Rogers stated that U.S. command over NATO forces, including nuclear weapons, is essential.
• Rep. Michael Turner, R-Ohio, expressed disbelief over discussions of relinquishing the Supreme Allied Command Europe (SACEUR) position.
• Katherine Thompson, acting assistant defense secretary for international affairs, confirmed that no decisions have been made regarding troop levels.
• Thompson denied that the U.S. would give up the SACEUR role, marking the first flat denial from Pentagon officials.
• There are approximately 100,000 U.S. troops in Europe, a 20,000-troop increase since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
• Army Gen. Christopher G. Cavoli recommended maintaining current troop levels to ensure military readiness.
• Cavoli warned that reducing troop levels would delay U.S. military response times to crises in Europe.
• Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., stated that any troop reduction would be a grave mistake and a sign of weakness.
• Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., criticized President Trump for empowering Russian President Vladimir Putin and urged continued U.S. support for Europe and Ukraine.
• Cavoli noted that NATO allies are increasing defense investments significantly since the war in Ukraine began.
• Thompson faced criticism for stating there is a ceasefire in Ukraine, which Rep. Smith refuted.
• Thompson struggled to address questions regarding Trump's favorable comments about Putin and his views on the Ukraine conflict.
• Thompson stated that the U.S. is urging NATO allies to increase their defense spending.
